applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: None currently in force for an offshore International Company structure; reliance on domestic legal protections and multilateral WTO commitments

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP, OFAC, UN, and domestic screening against the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit watchlist, Samoa Police watchlist, US OFAC SDN list, UK HMT consolidated list, EU consolidated list, and UN Security Council consolidated list; enhanced due diligence is triggered for all shareholders, directors, UBOs, and government counterparties in the medical ventilator procurement chain.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa Financial Services Authority International Companies e-Registry (https://www.fsa.gov.ws/ic-registry)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be submitted in English or Latin alphabet characters. If a Chinese or other non-Latin script name is required, a certified English transliteration must accompany the application. The official name must end with 'Limited', 'Ltd.', 'Corporation', 'Inc.', or a prescribed abbreviation. Samoan-language names are accepted only where not contrary to public policy and as otherwise provided by the Registrar.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 10 working days of a rejection notice by the Registrar of International Companies, the applicant may file a Notice of Appeal with the Registrar, attaching a fresh name search result, the rejected reservation reference, and a legal opinion addressing the objection. The Registrar must decide within 15 working days. An unsuccessful appeal may be renewed by way of judicial review before the Supreme Court of Samoa under the Judicature Ordinance 1961.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For an International Company engaged in medical ventilator manufacturing, a virtual office may be accepted solely for mailing and statutory agent purposes, but the company must maintain a physical business premises in Samoa or evidence of a licensed production facility and designated medical device controller; a purely virtual presence is non-compliant with the Samoa Medical Devices Regulations 2016.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), ss. 5-12 (Incorporation), s. 34 (Registered Office), s. 37 (Registered Agent)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), in conjunction with the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association together with Form IC-1 (Application for Incorporation of an International Company)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum issued or paid-up capital; no escrow or deposit account required; subscriber may adopt par value or no par value shares.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED, as the first resolution of the board of directors of WS-SAMOA ICU VENTILATOR MFG. LIMITED (the 'Company'), that: (1) the subscription of 1,000 ordinary shares of USD 1.00 each at par by the founding shareholder be and is hereby approved and accepted; (2) the registered office of the Company be fixed at the office of the licensed international company service provider in Apia, Samoa, and the service provider be appointed registered agent; (3) the undersigned be appointed as the first director, together with the appointment of a company secretary; and (4) the directors be and are hereby authorized to open bank accounts, execute statutory filings, and apply for all industrial, environmental and medical-device licences required for the manufacture of critical care ventilators. This resolution takes effect immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MCIL Companies Registry / SIFA electronic submission window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request through the authorized SIFA agent or the MCIL portal for the proposed corporate name, ensuring the name is not misleading, offensive, or identical to an existing domestic or international company. Attach a notarized consent letter from the sole shareholder and a short business-activity description.
required_dossiers: Business activity description for ICU ventilator manufacturing
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or flagged, file an amended name request within 14 days; provide additional supporting statement distinguishing the name from existing marks; no material fee for a first re-submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Memorandum and Articles of Association with Incorporation Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, MCIL / SIFA
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the Memorandum and Articles of Association before witnesses, complete Form IC-1, and lodge the entire dossier electronically or in hard copy at the Registrar's office. Confirm the registered office clause names the licensed Apia service provider in Samoa. Submit all documents in English and pay the prescribed filing fee by bank draft or government receipt.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association (signed and witnessed)
Form IC-1 (Application for Incorporation of an International Company)
Registered office and registered agent consent letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Upon a query or rejection notice from the Registrar, rectify the flagged document, execute a fresh signature page where needed, and re-lodge within 10 working days; any indexation or verification errors are cured by amended schedule submission without penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After satisfactory review, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation under the seal of the International Companies Registry. The Company must verify the certificate particulars (name, number, date of incorporation and liability clause) and download the certified copy from the registry portal.
required_dossiers: Identification and due-diligence dossier of founding shareholder and first director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate carries a typographical error or wrong date, submit a formal rectification request with an affidavit of correction; the Registrar re-issues the certificate within 5 working days at a nominal correction fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MCIL, Samoa Revenue Authority (SRA), and licensed international company service provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting or pass the first written resolution, adopt the registered office address, appoint directors and secretary, and open the statutory registers. Then register the Company with the SRA for the non-resident international company exemption certificate (if applicable), obtain a Business Licence approval letter, and file the registered agent's annual consent to act.
required_dossiers: First board resolution or written consent
Register of members, directors and secretary
Registered agent consent and government exemption application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the SRA or MCIL queries the governance documents, amend the register with a rectifying resolution and provide a certificate of good standing from the registered agent; late-filing penalties are waived if correction is completed within 15 days of first notice.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Business Licences Division
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Trade and Manufacturing Business Licence (Category: Manufacturing of Medical Devices)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA), Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category A Level 2 Full EIA Study (manufacturing operations with wastewater effluent, air emissions, and noise impacts)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Samoa National Water Quality Standards (trade wastewater pH 6.5-8.5, BOD < 50 mg/L) and the WHO Ambient Air Quality Guidelines for PM2.5, PM10 and VOCs; hazardous waste segregation per the Waste Management Regulations 2014, with disposal only through MNRE-approved contractors.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (SFESA) for the production premises; structural load inspection certificate from an MCIL-accredited professional engineer; workplace registration and OSH clearance under the Occupational Safety and Health Act 2002; Ministry of Health manufacturing-practice inspection for medical device production facility.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry for Revenue (Matagaluega o Tupe Maua), operating through the Samoa Revenue Authority (SRA); taxpayer e-Services portal at www.sra.gov.ws; customs clearance interface via Samoa Customs ASYCUDA World.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a non-resident-owned Samoa International Company, the licensed registered agent files incorporation with the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) and obtains the Certificate of Incorporation. The agent then files Form SRA-01 (Taxpayer Registration) with the Samoa Revenue Authority, enclosing the Certificate of Incorporation, memorandum and articles of association, registered agent certificate, particulars of directors and shareholders, and passport copies of beneficial owners. The SRA issues a 9-digit Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) in approximately 5-7 business days. The same TIN is used for VAGST, customs, PAYE, and business licence interactions. In parallel, the entity registers with Samoa Customs (ASYCUDA World) to obtain an importer/exporter code. If actual or expected taxable supplies exceed WST 100,000 in any consecutive 12-month period, the IC must file Form VG-1 for Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST) registration under the Goods and Services Tax Act 2007.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone. A Samoa International Company incorporated under the International Companies Act 1987 is a non-resident offshore-exempt vehicle: it is exempt from Samoan income tax, capital gains tax, and stamp duty on all income, profits, and transactions not sourced in Samoa, and it is not subject to entity-level taxation on global export manufacturing profits. No annual income tax return is required; the annual SIFA licence fee is the only state charge. The exemption is lost if the IC carries on business in Samoa, owns Samoan land, or transacts with Samoan residents in breach of the Act, in which case domestic resident-taxpayer rules apply.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch election exists in Samoa. Available statutory mechanisms include: (1) section 158 of the International Companies Act 1987 - conversion of an IC into a local company with Ministerial consent, changing the entity to resident, fully taxable status; (2) voluntary VAGST registration below the WST 100,000 threshold; (3) VAGST group registration and cash-basis accounting elections permitted by SRA determination for related and small enterprises; (4) customs warehouse licensing under the Customs Act 2014 allowing duty and VAGST deferral on imported ventilator components; (5) election to maintain accounting records in a foreign currency under the Tax Administration Act 2012. Absent hybrid-mismatch rules, the SRA applies general anti-avoidance, transfer-pricing, and thin-capitalisation (3:1 debt-to-equity) provisions to cross-border financing structures.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax (VAGST), a VAT-type consumption tax administered under the Goods and Services Tax Act 2007 and the Tax Administration Act 2012.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 100,000 (Samoan Tala) of taxable supplies in any consecutive 12-month period; a person commencing business must register if taxable turnover is reasonably expected to exceed WST 100,000 in the first 12 months; voluntary registration is permitted. A non-resident supplier is registerable only where it has a Samoan fixed establishment or otherwise supplies goods physically in Samoa.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or mandatory e-invoicing API regime is in force in Samoa. VAGST-registered suppliers must issue sequentially numbered VAGST tax invoices containing prescribed particulars (supplier name and TIN, VAGST registration number, invoice date, description, quantity, and price exclusive and inclusive of tax). Returns are filed electronically through the SRA taxpayer e-Services portal, and payments are cleared electronically. For exports, ASYCUDA World provides the electronic customs declaration and clearance platform; invoice-level real-time clearance by the tax authority is not mandated.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to goods exported by a registered VAGST person from Samoa to a destination outside Samoa, provided the goods are physically exported within 28 days of supply and the supplier retains documentary proof of export. Offshore services supplied to non-resident persons and performed entirely outside Samoa (including engineering, R&D, and assembly-support services for the ventilator line) are also zero-rated. The ventilator manufacturer receives a full input-tax credit on VAGST paid on imported components, circuit boards, sensors, and assembly machinery; where zero-rated outputs exceed taxable inputs, a cash refund is payable, subject to documentation checks.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (electronic ASYCUDA World declaration accepted by Samoa Customs)
Bill of Lading, Master Air Waybill, or through bill of lading evidencing physical export from Samoa
Commercial invoice and sequentially numbered VAGST zero-rated tax invoice
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) issued by the collecting Samoan commercial bank
SWIFT MT103 wire transfer advice or documentary letter-of-credit evidence of foreign-currency payment
Packing list, freight booking confirmation, and endorsed cargo movement record
Medical device export permit issued by the Samoa Ministry of Health where goods are classified as controlled health goods
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The SRA audits zero-rated export refund claims and may reopen assessments within the statutory period, which is extended without limit in cases of fraud. If goods are not exported within 28 days, or supporting documentation is incomplete or false, the SRA disallows zero-rating, assesses VAGST at 15% on the supply, and claws back any refund paid with statutory interest at 20% per annum. Penalty tax is imposed under the Tax Administration Act 2012: 100% of the tax shortfall for intentional misstatement, 50% for careless misstatement, 20% for minor errors, and 150% for deliberate evasion. Fraudulent evasion is a criminal offence punishable by a fine of up to WST 100,000 and/or imprisonment for a term of up to five years. The SRA may also deregister the exporter's VAGST number, disqualify the entity from future zero-rating, and refer the case to the Revenue Criminal Investigation Unit.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS), constituted under the Central Bank of Samoa Act 1984, exercising exchange-control administration under the Foreign Exchange Act 1975 and the Foreign Exchange Regulations 1976; enforcement is coordinated with the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2020 and with the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) which registers Samoa International Companies (WS_IC).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan Tala (WST) is convertible for bona fide current-account transactions through CBS-authorised dealers; capital-account movements (equity injections, cross-border loans, outward capital remittances) require CBS approval or a statutory exemption. A Samoa International Company conducting business exclusively in foreign currency with non-residents is outside the core exchange-control net under the International Companies Act 1987, permitting free maintenance and disposition of USD/EUR accounts. Convertibility friction materialises only where the IC transacts with Samoan residents in WST or remits to a resident beneficiary. Profit-remittance hurdles: dividends and capital distributions out of offshore foreign-currency earnings are remittable without a CBS licence, but the paying authorised dealer customarily requires a Samoa Revenue Authority (SRA) tax-clearance certificate, audited financial statements, and a board dividend resolution; remittances funded from resident-source WST receipts remain blocked unless CBS approval is obtained.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Statutory baseline: export proceeds must be credited to a Samoan account with an authorised dealer within 90 days of export and surrendered (converted to WST) at the prevailing market rate unless a CBS-approved retention account or exemption is granted. For WS_IC exporting ICU ventilators, the 90-day repatriation and conversion obligation is disapplied where the IC holds an exemption certificate confirming no resident business and maintains offshore USD collection accounts; if any export sale is settled in WST through a Samoan resident buyer, 100% of that WST receipt is subject to mandatory surrender. Operational protocol: obtain the CBS written exemption through the designated authorised dealer before first shipment and attach it to each export declaration; non-compliance exposes the IC to compulsory sale of foreign exchange, civil penalties up to twice the undeclared amount, and criminal liability under the Foreign Exchange Act 1975.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-Medium as primary clearing rail. Offshore digital EMIs (Airwallex, Currenxie, Wise Business, Mercury) cannot hold WST nor clear Samoa-domestic payment instruments, as CBS licenses only domestic banks and authorised financial institutions to operate payment and settlement systems. EMIs are viable solely as ancillary USD collection and concentration accounts feeding the licensed Samoan account, provided the EMI's upstream correspondent accepts the Samoan IC's full beneficial-ownership KYC. Legal constraint: EMIs cannot advise, issue, or settle commercial letters of credit or government instruments for Samoan public-health tenders; all LC and SIPS/WST-denominated flows must terminate at a CBS-licensed commercial bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is permitted by the leading Samoan banks for International Companies; directors are not statutorily required to appear physically in Apia provided (i) certified or apostilled board resolutions authorise the account and signatories, (ii) the KYC interview is completed by live video before a notary public or introducing bank officer, (iii) a licensed Samoan trust and company service provider (TCSP) acts as the bank's local verification correspondent, and (iv) each authorised signature is accompanied by a qualified legal practitioner's certification. ANZ Bank Samoa and BSP Samoa accept this remote route in practice; Samoa Commercial Bank may require one principal to attend in Apia for first account activation. All banks reserve the right to convene a physical interview within 90 days of onboarding if transaction patterns trigger enhanced due diligence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bearer-share or nominee-shareholder opacity flagged during beneficial-ownership verification under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2020.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified shareholder register issued by the registered agent; complete beneficial-ownership schedule tracing all natural persons; written confirmation that no bearer shares are outstanding; certificate of incorporation and current Annual Exemption Certificate; legal opinion from Samoan counsel confirming the ultimate ownership chain and compliance with FIU reporting obligations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Medical-device export exposure to sanctions-listed or high-risk jurisdictions triggering enhanced CDD and reputational review.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: WHO-format end-user certificates for each destination; export licence package under the Customs Act 2014; UN and OFAC sanctions screening logs of all customers and freight forwarders; ICC Incoterms 2020 sales contracts; ISO 13485 and WHO prequalification certificates; internal sanctions-compliance manual with audit trail and training records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unverified source of initial capital injection covering ventilator tooling and cleanroom capex, classed as unexplained wealth.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 24-month bank statements of the funding shareholder; audited financial statements of the group; tax-clearance certificates from the funding jurisdiction; sworn declaration of source of wealth; third-party valuation report of contributed machinery and intellectual property; traceable board resolution recording the capital contribution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-exempt International Company structure red-flagged as potential tax evasion or round-tripping in the banking review.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: International Company certificate of incorporation; current PER (Exemption) Certificate confirming offshore foreign-currency status; economic-substance board pack evidencing genuine export operations; CbCR and EOIR filings where applicable; legal nexus memorandum demonstrating real cross-border trade in ICU ventilators with non-resident counterparties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficiary-name mismatch between the government tender award and the bank account holder when receiving Ministry of Health LC proceeds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised confirmation of beneficial entitlement signed by the procuring ministry; government award letter; registered-supplier certificate; IC extract matching the registered legal name exactly; written verification from the issuing bank's correspondent confirming the trade is bona fide; purchase order and proforma invoice referencing the identical corporate name.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing: the originating shareholder bank transmits a SWIFT MT103 to ANZ Bank Samoa or BSP Samoa for crediting the IC's USD account in Apia. The wire must carry the IC's registered corporate name exactly, the ICSL file number, reference the board capital-contribution resolution, and cite the CBS-designated purpose code for foreign direct investment in the beneficiary-to-beneficiary information field. The receiving authorised dealer holds funds for one to two days pending source-of-funds verification before final credit; any WST conversion is executed only on a CBS Foreign Exchange Declaration (EA01) filed by the authorised dealer. Retain the contribution resolution, updated share register, CBS declaration receipt, and bank credit advice for subsequent audit and for the SRA tax-clearance file.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 for supplier pre-payments and general trade transfers, referencing the invoice and proforma packing list; (ii) Commercial Letters of Credit (MT700) advised through ANZ or BSP for high-value ventilator component consignments, with documents presented strictly under UCP 600; (iii) Government settlement via the Samoa Ministry of Health using a government LC or direct payment order/MT203 to the IC's account upon delivery acceptance; (iv) same-day local WST clearing through the CBS-operated Samoa Interbank Payment System (SIPS) for Samoa-denominated operational costs. Each outbound disbursement requires a complete packet comprising commercial invoice, bill of lading or airway bill, packing list, insurance certificate, and underlying purchase order, with all documents aligned to the declared CBS purpose code; disbursements to unauthorised third-country beneficiaries trigger mandatory CBS reporting.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: WST/USD deliverable forward contracts up to 12 months executed through CBS-authorised dealers for bona fide trade transactions
Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on the Samoan Tala entered into with non-resident banks where no local hedging market depth exists
USD/AUD and USD/EUR cross-currency swaps with authorised dealers to align ventilator import-component and export-tender currencies

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: International Company Annual Renewal and Government Fee (Annual License/Franchise Maintenance)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fixed calendar deadline: on or before 30 June each year; no incorporation-anniversary election; the statutory fee is prescribed in Samoan tala and approximates USD 185 at prevailing exchange rates.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unpaid fee attracts a prescribed late penalty (typically 10%); continued non-payment for 3 months after the due date permits the Registrar to issue a strike-off notice, and administrative dissolution follows if restoration and arrears payment are not completed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Registered Agent Declaration and Beneficial Ownership Confirmation (Annual Return of Members and Directors)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies via licensed Samoan registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due with the 30 June renewal; also due within 14 days after any share transfer, change of directors, secretary, registered office, or beneficial owner.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Continuing offence under the International Companies Act 2012; statutory monetary penalties and daily default fines may be imposed on the company and each director; non-compliance for more than 3 months after Registrar notice may be treated as grounds for administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Statutory Register Audit Certification by Registered Agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registered Agent (record maintained at the registered office; certification incorporated in the annual renewal declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Completed before the 30 June renewal; updated immediately after each board or shareholder meeting.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Defective or unavailable statutory registers subject the company and officers to offence penalties; the Registrar may direct an inspection and strike off the company for continued or egregious non-maintenance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory audit thresholds based on revenue, assets, or employees for a Samoa International Company. A mandatory independent audit arises only if the company's constitution requires it, members pass a special resolution requiring it, or the Registrar/SIFA orders an audit in an enforcement context.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (IASB standards as accepted in Samoa) if audited financial statements are prepared; a non-resident International Company is not required to file financial statements with the Registrar. Records must be sufficient to explain transactions and financial position and be retained at the registered office for 7 years.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each share transfer requires an executed instrument of transfer and board approval; the transfer is recorded in the Register of Members and the UBO register is updated within 14 days. During the annual 30 June renewal, the registered agent obtains a directors' confirmation of current members and beneficial owners; a company with unchanged ownership remains covered by the previous confirmation but must expressly reconfirm to satisfy AML/CFT record-keeping.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350 - 850 per annum (licensed registered agent, registered office, and resident secretary)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 - 9,000 per voluntarily appointed certified audit; no audit is required for tax-exempt International Company renewal

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% for an International Company under the Samoa International Companies tax-exempt offshore regime; resident domestic companies carrying on business in Samoa are taxed at the 27% corporate income tax rate under the Income Tax Act 2018.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Full statutory exemption from Samoan income tax, stamp duty and exchange control for International Companies; no capital gains tax on IC asset disposals; no Samoan withholding tax on IC distributions; the only annual fiscal charge is the fixed government license fee (WST 500 to WST 2,500 depending on IC category).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: International Company Annual Return and Declaration of Compliance (Form IC-AR) filed with the Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia, Samoa; electronic filing and annual fee payment are processed through the MCIL International Companies e-Registry portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, regardless of whether the International Company derived any income during the year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due on or before the anniversary of the date of registration/incorporation each year; a 30-day grace period is available only upon payment of the statutory late fee; no extension exists for tax-exempt ICs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company legal name and certificate of incorporation registration number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the exact name and registration number as shown on the Certificate of Incorporation; non-resident beneficial ownership details are not required on this form.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered office street address in Samoa and licensed registered agent particulars.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A licensed Samoa-registered agent must countersign; a post office box is not acceptable as the registered office address.
List all directors; at least one natural person director is required, but non-resident directors and corporate directors are permitted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Issued share capital and registered shareholder register summary.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders may hold 100% of the shares; bearer shares are prohibited and must be dematerialized.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Principal business activity, ISIC v4 code and activity description.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For the ventilator manufacturing scope, state 'ISIC 3250 - Manufacture of medical and surgical equipment, including turbine-driven intensive care ventilators'; certify that all customers are non-residents of Samoa.
Certify that the IC has not carried on business with Samoan residents, has not acquired Samoan land, and has not derived Samoan-source income in the filing period.
Indicate whether the IC undertakes a relevant activity under the International Companies (Economic Substance) Act 2020; if yes, a separate Economic Substance Return is required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Annual government license fee schedule and remittance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Pay the fixed WST 500-2,500 fee by bank wire to the MCIL collection account; the fee is flat and unrelated to revenue or profit.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing surcharge of WST 500 for each month or part of a month (maximum WST 5,000); continued default for six months triggers automatic strike-off of the IC and forfeiture of the company name; false declarations attract criminal penalties under the Declarations law and the International Companies Act 1987.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Economic Substance Return (Form ESR-1) filed with the Samoa International Companies Registry (MCIL) in accordance with the International Companies (Economic Substance) Act 2020 and the International Companies (Economic Substance) Regulation 2021.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, within 12 months after the accounting reference date (financial year-end).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due on or before the last day of the 12th month following the financial year-end; a further extension is not automatic and must be applied for before the normal due date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Classify among banking, insurance, shipping, fund management, financing and leasing, headquarters, holding company, intellectual property holder, or distribution and service centre; an ICU ventilator manufacturer exporting to foreign hospitals should declare 'distribution and service centre' unless it qualifies as 'headquarters'.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income sourced from Samoa for the accounting period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report zero for a pure offshore IC except for nominal administrative income; figures must reconcile with the IC's bank statements and audited accounts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenditure incurred in Samoa (rent, payroll, utilities, professional fees).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenditure must be materially adequate relative to the declared activity; token annual spending below WST 5,000 will be treated by the Registrar as a substance failure.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Number of full-time employees physically working in Samoa.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only employees performing management or core-income-generating functions while physically in Samoa count; overseas remote employees do not satisfy substance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Physical office or premises in Samoa.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the street address and floor area; a virtual mailbox without a physical local office is insufficient for non-holding relevant activities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Core income-generating activities (CIGAs) performed in Samoa.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State where procurement, manufacturing contracts, invoicing, treasury functions and key venture-risk decisions occur; board minutes, contracts and invoices must evidence that these CIGAs are directed from Samoa.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Board meeting details (date, venue, quorum and minutes location).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Hold at least one physical or virtual board meeting per year in Samoa for distribution/service companies, and quarterly meetings for IP-holding companies; minutes must record strategic decisions made in Samoa.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Initial penalty of WST 50,000 for non-filing or false filing plus WST 10,000 per month of continuing default; automatic exchange of information with treaty partners and the EU Code of Conduct Group; the Registrar may strike off the IC and disqualify the registered agent.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% on dividends and distributions paid by an International Company, because the IC is a tax-exempt offshore entity outside the Samoan income tax net; the domestic statutory dividend WHT of 15% applies only where a resident Samoan company pays dividends to a non-resident under the Income Tax Act 2018.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Where a Samoan resident payer is involved, the non-resident recipient must file a Treaty Relief Request with the Samoa Ministry of Revenue before or within 12 months of payment, attaching: (i) a Certificate of Residence (TRC) from the payer's Samoan tax office, (ii) a valid TRC from the recipient's residence country, and (iii) a 10%+ ownership declaration to access the reduced direct-investment dividend rate; Samoa's DTA network (Australia, New Zealand and select Pacific states) caps portfolio dividend WHT at 15% and substantial-holding dividends at 5%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory rates: 15% WHT on royalties and 15% WHT on interest paid by a Samoan resident payer to a non-resident; treaty rates typically 10% for both royalties and interest under Samoa's negotiated DTAs, subject to TRC and beneficial-ownership certification; payments made by an exempt International Company carry no Samoan WHT obligation because the payer is not subject to Samoan income tax.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File (contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation) is mandatory where related-party transactions exceed WST 5,000,000 in a tax year; Master File is required where offshore group consolidated revenue exceeds WST 100,000,000 or where the group files a Samoan consolidated return; tax-exempt International Companies are excluded from income tax transfer pricing documentation unless they unlawfully carry on business with Samoan residents.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The International Companies (Economic Substance) Act 2020 requires every Samoa International Company undertaking a relevant activity to demonstrate in Samoa: (i) effective management and control, (ii) adequate physical premises, (iii) adequate qualified employees, and (iv) adequate operating expenditure proportionate to profit. A turbine-driven ICU ventilator manufacturer operating through an IC, holding IP, or earning service and distribution income must satisfy this test; a pure equity holding exemption is available only where the IC performs no active trading and holds only passive investments.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Prohibited Domestic Dealings
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Certifying false offshore status while selling ICU mechanical ventilators to Samoan hospitals, engaging a Samoan resident as local distributor, deriving Samoan-source income, or holding Samoan land while claiming the International Company exemption.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Strike-off and loss of International Company status; retrospective assessment as a resident taxpayer at 27% corporate tax on all Samoan-source income, plus penalty tax up to 150% of the shortfall and interest at 10% per annum under the Income Tax Act 2018; company fines up to WST 100,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the registered agent who signed the false annual return are jointly and severally liable for unpaid tax, penalties and interest; criminal conviction for tax evasion carries imprisonment up to 7 years, personal fines up to WST 50,000, a travel ban pending tax clearance, and disqualification from acting as a director in Samoa.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Economic Substance Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating with no physical presence in Samoa, no local employees, no board meetings held in Samoa, and no substantive records, while filing a holding-company exemption; failing to file the Economic Substance Return within 12 months of the financial year-end; responding to the Registrar's substance questionnaire with zero activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: WST 50,000 penalty plus WST 10,000 per month of continuing default; strike-off and forfeiture of IC assets; automatic exchange of information with EU Member States and Global Forum members; referral for transitional listing as a non-cooperative jurisdiction where systemic failures persist.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable to pay substance penalties where the company defaults, face disqualification from the Samoa company registry for up to 5 years, and, for shell structures used to evade foreign tax, may be subjected to mutual-assistance travel bans and extradition proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and False Invoicing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Under-invoicing ventilator exports or turbine component imports between related entities, using government LC and SWIFT corridors to shift profit to a no-tax jurisdiction, creating artificial losses for the Samoan manufacturer, or failing to prepare contemporaneous arm's-length documentation above the WST 5,000,000 threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income adjustment to the arm's length price under anti-avoidance rules; 27% corporate tax on the adjusted amount plus penalty of up to 150% and interest; cancellation of the IC tax-exemption certificate; referral to the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit for trade-based money-laundering investigation; fines up to WST 100,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false cross-border invoices face criminal liability for false accounting under the Samoa Criminal Law Act with imprisonment up to 5 years, and each knowingly participating director is liable up to WST 100,000 for the resulting tax shortfall.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering and Corruption in Government Procurement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying kickbacks to hospital procurement officials to secure government LC-backed ventilator purchase contracts, structuring payments through nominee accounts or shell vendors, receiving third-party funds without invoice backing, or failing to conduct KYC on end-users and counterparties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Offences under the Anti-Money Laundering and Proceeds of Crime Act 2018: fines up to WST 1,000,000, confiscation of the ventilator shipments and proceeds, freeze and forfeiture orders, permanent vendor blacklisting from Samoan government procurement, and imprisonment up to 14 years for money laundering.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, beneficial owners and the registered agent are jointly liable for restitution of corrupt payments; travel bans and asset restraint orders issue automatically upon charge; individual sentencing may reach 14 years' imprisonment and permanent exclusion from public procurement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Medical Device Regulatory and Licensing Violations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Manufacturing, importing or exporting turbine-driven ICU mechanical ventilators without the required Ministry of Health medical device license, lacking WHO/ISO quality certification, or shipping devices falsely declared under a different tariff line to obtain preferential customs treatment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Seizure and destruction of non-compliant devices; customs penalty up to 200% of the goods' duty-paid value; revocation of the exporter license; referral to the medical products regulator; public disclosure of the enforcement action.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face personal fines up to WST 250,000 and criminal liability for endangering public health with imprisonment up to 10 years where devices fail life-safety standards; travel bans may be imposed pending investigation, and directors leaving Samoa remain subject to extradition under mutual assistance treaties.
